_comment: The Stones Are Dimming, Act V: The Ashen Scar (finale) and the homecoming. All four mechanics at once. Story v2: allies arrive by your earlier choices (Tuskridge, goblins, the herd or Thistle, Corin, Bram, Wren). At the mouth, 'All of them' pours in every ember you helped lay; who else pays is decided by line priority in seal_count (hidden Kindled Dawn > Bram, if spared > Tamsin, if pardoned > Idra) and recorded as r1.ending.*. Format: see r1_act1.json.

lines.text: Edge rules: pay, eat, don't die. You don't look like you came to pay.
An ash-reader. Fine. I bought crystal. I paid boys to cut stones. I'd do it again.
Corin told you, did he? Good lad. Bad spy. Yes. I paid. I'd do it again.
Hollin's Reach. My village. The Crown pulled the ward-lines back and left us outside.
Bram's in a Crown cell? Good. ...No. Nothing's good. He did the sum. I did the burying.
You let Bram walk? Then he's out there hauling stone like it helps. He did the sum. I did the burying.
Forty graves, one winter. So I let the dark pay, for once. Pay the people it ate.

choices.text: Help us end it. Then we talk.

lines.text: Fair. Take the anchor stone anyway. Edge rules: pay your debts, even to Kings.
Talk. Ha. Here's the anchor stone. Lay it right, and I'll fight at your side.
The tide runs back to the mouth. Burn and ward, cell by cell. Don't chase it. Walk it home.
Runeward crews crest the ridge behind you, hauling fresh stone and singing badly.
Tuskridge war-horns on the ridge. Harrok's clan comes down the scree, roaring your name.
Goblins in the rocks. Snikkit points and shrieks: purple there! And there! And THERE!
The Stagborn come down the old ward-line, Thistle at their head, antlers blazing. The violet backs away.
Thistle plants all four hooves beside you and refuses, absolutely, to be anywhere else.
A Crown cart: Corin Vesk, released for the day. Same chisel, he says. Other way round.
Corin Vesk is with the Runeward crews. He carves like he's apologising to every stone.
Corin brings six Ashen Hand cutters. We know which ones are failing, he says. So we fix those first.
No sign of Bram Hollis. In Kingsreach, a cell door stays shut.
At the back, hauling stone, a grey man who won't meet your eyes. Bram Hollis.
Miss me? Don't answer that. Left flank's mine.
Something vast stands up out of the violet. Stone skin. Crystal spine. It was a troll, once.
It's a troll now, too. A worse one. I'll take the left.
It's down. The mouth is still open. It wants an ember to close it.
Mine. I'm old, I'm ready, and frankly I'd like the view. I've been practising for thirty years.
Good. Keep the chisel sharp. And for pity's sake, throw out that tea.
Maren's saving me a seat. She'll cheat at staves. Go home, love.
All of... the lines. You routed them here. Every heart in the Vale is...
We are here. Miller, knight, grandmother, one-armed teacher. Stand aside, Warden.
The embers pour in. The mouth shrinks, then sticks, a hand's width open. It wants one living ember.
The mouth shrinks, then sticks, a hand's width open. It wants one living ember. Tamsin drops her pack.
The mouth shrinks, then sticks, a hand's width open. It wants one living ember. Bram is already walking.
A Stagborn bellow. The herd walks the lines in, an orc-mother roars, a lantern for nobody flares. It shuts.
Hush. I was going anyway, love. Now I get to go somewhere useful.
Edge rules: pay your debts. Tell my brother the sum came out even.
Nine guards. Forty-one stones. Sixty miles. One of me. That sum, I can do.
Tell your father I was a good captain, once. He'll know when.
Staff up, lantern-holder. Nobody else pays tonight. Not one.
As the mouth closes, you see past it: a red sky raining fire, and a violet forest breathing light.
You're home. You're home and you're whole. Sit. Eat. Then tell me absolutely everything.
You're home and you're whole. Sit. Eat. And get that stag off my roof.
Heard. The Miller's Stone was singing when I passed it. Never once did that for me.
Kindling Night, a year on. New lanterns at the ring: Maren. Rowan. Idra Vell, who'd hate the fuss.
Kindling Night, a year on. New lanterns: Maren. Rowan. And one nobody signs. Everybody knows whose.
Kindling Night, a year on. New lanterns: Maren. Rowan. Tamsin Reeve, of Hollin's Reach.
Kindling Night, a year on. Two new lanterns: Maren, Rowan. Idra hangs a third, for the ones with nobody.
I'm retiring. The chisel is yours. The tea, regrettably, is also yours.
The Staff Yard has twelve new strays. I knock them all over. It's tradition now.
The little lantern-holder. Look how tall. Go on, then. Live. We've got the road.
A new voice on the wind, from the Scar: Warden Vell, on watch. The tea is terrible here too.
From the Scar, a tired voice, counting: nine, forty-one, sixty, one. Even, at last.
From the Scar: Edge rules. Debt paid. Tell Hollin's Reach I'm home.
From the Scar, no single voice. The whole Vale humming, like a hive in summer.
Staff up, lantern-holder. ...Hm. Not bad. Not good. Not bad.
